articles.title: Circular economy & resource recovery: From policy direction to industrial material flow transformation
articles.summary: The article explores how India's shift from linear to circular economic systems depends not just on sustainability goals but on industrial capabilities to recover and reuse resources. It argues that future industrial leadership will favor nations that maximize resource retention, implying a need for policy and industrial strategies to support this transition. The piece is framed as a commentary on industrial transformation rather than a report on specific government actions.
articles.raw_summary: The transition from linear to circular systems is not a question of sustainability ambition alone. It is a question of industrial capability. The next phase of industrial leadership will belong not to those who consume the most resources, but to those who recover and retain them most effectively.

articles.title: Vietnam proposes banning under-16s from posting on social media
articles.summary: Vietnam's government is proposing to ban children under 16 from posting on social media without parental supervision. Social media platforms would need to verify users' ages and restrict content for minors. The plan also includes limits on daily online gaming time for children. This move aligns with growing global concerns about protecting children's online safety and digital well-being.

These proposals reflect growing global concerns about children's online safety.

articles.title: Why oil prices haven't gone crazy despite 5 months of US-Iran war
articles.summary: Oil prices remained relatively stable despite five months of US-Iran conflict, peaking at $126 per barrel—well below the 2008 high of $147. Brent crude averaged $101 between February 28 and June 11, when the US called off strikes, before dropping to $70 in early July. The conflict raises concerns for India, a major oil importer, due to potential supply disruptions and price volatility affecting fuel costs and inflation.

articles.title: US appeals court blocks part of Texas children's online safety law
articles.summary: A US appeals court in New Orleans blocked part of Texas' Securing Children Online through Parental Empowerment Act (SCOPE Act) in a 2-1 decision. articles.summary: The Indian government's Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) ordered GitHub to remove a Bluetooth-based chat app called Bitchat, citing security risks. The order highlights concerns over unregulated digital communication tools and their potential impact on national security and lawful interception.

The move highlights ongoing discussions around FDI regulations in India's digital economy.

Following this, Blinkit moved to an inventory model from a pure marketplace model earlier.

Key provisions include mandatory completion of investigations within two months, the establishment of special fast-track courts for offenses, and day-to-day trials to be concluded within three months of chargesheet filing. The bill aims to strengthen accountability and expedite legal proceedings in cases of exam malpractice.
